title: 2027 Toyota Tundra Hybrid Pricing, Specs, and Release Date
summary: The 2027 Toyota Tundra Hybrid features revised exterior styling, an updated infotainment system, and the latest version of Toyota’s driver-assistance package.
body_markdown:
The Toyota Tundra Hybrid is a full-size pickup truck with bold styling, plenty of power, and hardcore off-road capability. It competes primarily with the Ford F-150, the Chevrolet Silverado 1500, and the Ram 1500.

## What’s New for the 2027 Toyota Tundra Hybrid


The 2027 Toyota Tundra Hybrid full-size pickup truck boasts revised exterior styling, an updated infotainment system, the latest version of Toyota’s standard active safety and driver-assistance package, and other assorted new toys. The TRD Pro trim will be available with an exclusive new Honeycomb exterior paint color and also gets red tow hooks and Fox shocks. The new Trailhunter package that’s available for gas-powered 2027 Tundra models is exclusive to SR5 trim and therefore won’t be available with the Tundra Hybrid.


## Design


The Tundra Hybrid is available with a choice of Double Cab and CrewMax cabs and three different bed lengths. It’s refreshed for 2027 with a new-look front end comprising bumper-integrated rectangular fog lights and a brighter LED light bar. Available front recovery hooks and Rigid off-road fog lights contribute to both the rugged style and functionality. The Tundra Hybrid comes standard with 20-inch wheels in its lowest Limited trim level, but it’s available with 22-inch wheels or 18-inch wheels with all-terrain tires depending on spec.


## Powertrain


The Tundra Hybrid features Toyota’s i-Force Max hybrid powertrain, which improves both fuel economy and acceleration compared to the base engine, but it’s only available in the Tundra’s higher trim levels. It features an electric motor situated between the V6 engine and a 10-speed automatic transmission, providing 583 pound-feet of torque and a hefty 437 horsepower. The Tundra handles well for a big truck, with responsive steering, a reasonably smooth ride, and minimal body lean. The Tundra Hybrid is rated for 22 mpg combined with RWD and 20 mpg combined with 4WD.


## Interior


Both Double Cab and CrewMax versions of the Tundra Hybrid seat five across their two rows. The CrewMax model is the better option for families or big groups, with rear legroom that nearly matches that in front. Standard features include synthetic leather upholstery and power-adjustable front seats with heating and ventilation. Options include a panoramic roof, leather upholstery, a heated steering wheel, driver’s seat memory settings, heated and ventilated rear seats, walnut trim, and power-retractable running boards.


## Technology


The 2027 Tundra Hybrid features an updated version of Toyota’s infotainment software, with all versions now using a 14-inch touchscreen. Other standard features include a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity, and a built-in dash cam system that automatically or manually records 20-second video clips from the Tundra’s camera network. The Tundra Hybrid is offered with a 2.4-kW inverter that can power small appliances and equipment, such as tools or camping gear.

## Safety


The Tundra Hybrid uses an updated version of the Toyota Safety Sense package, TSS 4.0, for 2027. It adds features such as a pre-collision preparation system, adaptive cruise control, and Proactive Driving Assist, which can gently brake and steer the vehicle automatically. The Tundra Hybrid also gets a surround-view camera system, forward collision warning, forward automatic emergency braking, pedestrian detection, and front and rear parking sensors. The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety awarded the 2026 Tundra a Top Safety Pick rating, and it received a five-star overall safety rating from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. The 2027 Tundra Hybrid hadn't been evaluated at the time of writing.


## Pricing and Release Date


Toyota hadn't published pricing for the 2027 Tundra Hybrid at the time of writing, and full details are due later in the year. As a reference, the 2026 Tundra Hybrid lineup starts at $58,560 and goes up to $80,800. These prices do not include Toyota’s $2,195 handling fee for 2026 Tundra models.
